newsitem.title: POLAND: New flood will not damage more Polish crops - min.
newsitem.headline: New flood will not damage more Polish crops - min.

text.p: New floods may hit southern Poland after expected heavy rain on Thursday night but they will mostly affect areas already flooded and should not cause more damage to crops, a deputy agriculture minister said.

Jerzy Pilarczyk told Reuters in an interview that so far 120,000 hectares of grain fields had been destroyed which was likely to cut this year's grain output by 480,000 tonnes, mainly spring wheat and barley and to a lesser extent rye.
"The potential new flood wave will affect the same areas that have already been under water," Pilarczyk said.

"The already-incurred losses are not likely to influence the country's grain balance because harvests look even better than last year and Poland has 1.5 million tonnes more grain reserves than last year," he said.
In 1996 Poland produced 24.73 million tonnes of grain and analysts see its reserves this year at 4-4.5 million tonnes. Domestic consumption is between 25 and 26 million tonnes.
Pilarczyk said there would be no need for additional grain imports and he did not expect prices to rise.
Weather forecasts say up to 70 mm of rain in 24 hours may fall on the northern Czech Republic and parts of Poland's southern provinces starting Thursday night, possibly causing a second deluge.

The first flood inundated more than 4,000 sq km, killing at least 46 people and forcing tens of thousands of out their homes in 10 days. At it worst last week, rainfall was 140-150 mm a day but experts warn that lands already satured by the previous flood wave will not be able to absorb as much water and rivers were already at or above danger levels.
"We expect a large rise in the water level and the flood wave may again hit the town of Opole and Wroclaw, but this time we are better prepared for it," Pilarczyk said.
He said local flood relief committees were already repairing dykes and pumps in endangered areas and the government has sent troops to reinforce them.
There are no financial estimates of the damage done by the first flood yet but the government is lining up some four billion zlotys to deal with its effect. --Anthony Barker +48 22 653 9700
